seat.BEST_WHY: The light is occluded geometry, not a radial gradient. Sampling luminance in a ring around the figure at (408, 485): at r=160px the values are SW 174, NE 157, SE 43, N 9 — the bright arms point exactly down the open floor and up the corridor, the dark arms sit behind the wall run at y 383–455. A blob filter cannot produce that. The histogram backs it: p99 of the play area is 200 with a max of 250, so a small hot core sits on top of a lit field that is otherwise the same value as image 1's — that is what a carried lamp does, a tight core and a long roll-off. Second: the wall run directly above the figure has a stepped top silhouette rather than a ruled one — the black edge drops at x≈500 and steps up again at x≈445, and two driven timbers at x≈290 and x≈355 cross the top course and overhang it by 3–4px, so the run reads as a line that has been patched at different times rather than a stamped course. Third, at 9× the floor slab at (200–290, 455–520) is genuine hard-edged pixel work — the crack is a 1px black run with single-pixel jogs, and the hatch scratches differ slab to slab. No blur anywhere in the source art; the softness is the light layer only.
seat.WORST_WHY: The water is a literal rectangle. I measured its left and right edges at every tenth row from y=0 to y=191: x=248 and x=343 on every single row, no exception. Ninety-six pixels wide, exactly six tiles, with no shoreline, no edge tile, no depth change, no bank. It ends at the dirt on a 1px vertical cut. The dirt-to-stone boundary along the bottom is the same failure: first grey pixel at y=216 for every x from 60 through 235, a dead rule with no transition. There is no lighting of any kind — the four frame corners sample to luminance 90, 90, 90, 90. The two yellow crates at (63–98, 0–19) and (63–98, 48–67) are 86% pixel-identical (690 of 800 pixels exactly equal, max channel difference 31), i.e. the same sprite stamped twice with a tint nudge. The crates and the barrels at (113–199, 190–218) are drawn in a three-quarter view with visible front faces and staves, sitting on a floor drawn straight down. The bone scatter at (207–233, 110–128) is loose near-white pixels with no silhouette — it reads as dirt on the screen, not an object. The wall stub at (0–57, 122–145) with the orange post below it connects to nothing and terminates in mid-dirt.
seat.FLAGGED:
3, 2, 1

- **3** — the rectangular pond and the flat, sourceless light.
- **2** — the light is overcooked. p99 is 231 against 4's 200 on identical art; the floor slabs at (300–480, 455–500) lose their joint lines entirely into the glow, and a pale halo sits directly under the black occlusion line at the wall base from x≈300 to x≈480, which reads as bloom, not as lamplight on stone.
- **1** — the lamp has no core. Peak luminance anywhere in the play area is 223 against 250 in 2 and 4, and p99 is 198, so the lit pool is a single broad even wash. The result is that the frame reads as an ambient-lit room with a vignette rather than a figure carrying the only light. Compounding it: because the wall run sits one tile further back here (y 418–455 instead of 383–455), the light climbs its face — luminance due north of the figure at r=80 is 124 in image 1 versus 50 in 2 and 4 — and what it lights up is roughly two tiles of undifferentiated mottled fill with a single unbroken horizontal joint ruled edge to edge beneath it.

flip_list: Everything in FLIP 4 — same scene, same pier, same shadowless block.

The lamp has no core: max 223, p99 198, so core and field are nearly the same value. Add a tight bright core in the ~1.5 tiles around (408, 485) — 4 reaches 250 there over an equivalent field — so the figure reads as the light source.

Move the wall run above the figure back to y≈383 (where 2 and 4 have it) or drop the light that reaches its face. As it stands, luminance north of the figure at r=80 is 124 and the light fully reveals two tiles of blank fill.

The wall run's top joint is one unbroken horizontal rule from x=190 to x=505 at constant depth. Break it: vary the joint depth along the run and step the course at least twice, so the stones read as cut and set rather than stamped.
The wall run's top silhouette is a straight edge across its whole width. Give it the notch-and-return treatment the same wall has in 4 at x≈445–500.
Where the horizontal wall meets the corridor wall at x≈505, the two runs meet at a flush T at different course heights with no corner return. Resolve the corner.

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.

law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.

Thirteen 20-row bands down x505..580: 23.34 at r=285px, 28.56, 32.93, 42.74, 46.01, 57.39, 66.36, 83.67, 94.53, 104.48, 109.89 at r=85px - twelve of thirteen steps are toward the lamp, and there is no interior maximum. _what: THE ROUND CLOSED FAIL AND IS AMENDED TO INSTALL-LATEST. Recorded here because the
enforcement of a disposition is VISIBILITY - what is not written down cannot be audited
'No unrouted flags' is evaluated at two points (SKILL.md). At ROUND time it means the
seat did not flag the build, and seat 2 did, so the panel returned FAIL - correctly.
The second point is the gate, where each flagged item carries a disposition. That
amendment was a human-only act until 2026-09-08; the autonomy amendment moved ROUTED to
the builder BY VERIFIED CITATION, and left CLOSED and PARKED with Rafe.
Nothing here is asserted. critic_gate re-derives the majority from panel.per_seat, the
exit from item_exit.measured, and every citation against the record; a citation that
does not resolve is refused by machine. Amending moves this verdict from a state with no
checks left to run into the strictest one the gate has.
